request: show why a triangle's area is half base times height

beats.narration: Start with a rectangle, six wide and three tall: eighteen square units.
beats.code:
stage.title("Half base times height")
rect = draw_polygon(stage, [(-3, -1.5), (3, -1.5), (3, 1.5), (-3, 1.5)], color=GREY_B, fill=0.1)
stage.label((0, -1.5), "base 6", direction=DOWN)
stage.label((3, 0), "height 3", direction=RIGHT)

beats.intent: A triangle inside it with its apex on the top edge, the two leftover pieces shaded
beats.narration: Draw a triangle on the same base, with its tip on the top edge. The parts outside it are two smaller triangles.
beats.code:
tri = draw_polygon(stage, [(-3, -1.5), (3, -1.5), (-1, 1.5)], color=BLUE, fill=0.5)
left = Polygon([-3, -1.5, 0], [-1, 1.5, 0], [-3, 1.5, 0], color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.4)
right = Polygon([3, -1.5, 0], [3, 1.5, 0], [-1, 1.5, 0], color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.4)
stage.play(FadeIn(left), FadeIn(right))
stage.add(left, right)
alt = draw_line(stage, (-1, 1.5), (-1, -1.5), color=YELLOW, dashed=True)

beats.intent: Each orange piece matched by an equal blue piece across the dashed height line
beats.narration: The height line splits the triangle into two parts, each exactly matching an orange piece. So the triangle is half the rectangle.
beats.code:
stage.play(Indicate(left), Indicate(Polygon([-3, -1.5, 0], [-1, -1.5, 0], [-1, 1.5, 0])))
stage.play(Indicate(right), Indicate(Polygon([-1, -1.5, 0], [3, -1.5, 0], [-1, 1.5, 0])))
stage.equation(r"A = \tfrac12 \times 6 \times 3", r"= 9")

beats.intent: 60 at the top splitting into 6 and 10
beats.narration: Sixty splits into six times ten.

beats.intent: 6 splitting into 2 and 3, 10 into 2 and 5, the primes circled
beats.narration: Six is two times three; ten is two times five. Two, three and five are prime: they can't split further.
Collect the primes at the ends of the branches: sixty is two squared times three times five, and no other set of primes multiplies to sixty.

request: explain how a print queue works

beats.intent: A printer box on the left and three documents A, B, C lined up in the order they were sent
beats.narration: Three documents are sent to a printer: A first, then B, then C. They wait in a queue.
beats.code:
stage.title("A print queue")
printer = draw_rectangle(stage, width=1.6, height=1.2, color=GREY_B, fill=0.6)
printer.move_to([-4.5, 0, 0])
stage.label(printer, "printer", direction=DOWN)
docs = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=0.8, height=1.0, color=c, fill_opacity=0.6) for c in (BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3).move_to([-1.5, 0, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(d, shift=LEFT) for d in docs], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(docs)
names = [Text(n, font_size=30).move_to(d) for d, n in zip(docs, "ABC")]
stage.play(*[FadeIn(t) for t in names])
for d, t in zip(docs, names):
    d.add(t)

beats.intent: A document D joining the back of the queue while A goes into the printer
beats.narration: A new document D joins at the back. Meanwhile the one at the front, A, goes to the printer.
beats.code:
new = Rectangle(width=0.8, height=1.0, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([3.5, 0, 0])
new.add(Text("D", font_size=30).move_to(new))
stage.play(FadeIn(new, shift=LEFT))
stage.play(new.animate.next_to(docs[-1], RIGHT, buff=0.3), docs[0].animate.move_to(printer).scale(0.6))
stage.add(new)
stage.caption("join at the back, leave from the front")

beats.intent: The queue moving up: B at the front, then C, then D
beats.narration: Everyone moves up one place. First in, first out: documents print in the order they arrived.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeOut(docs[0]), FadeOut(names[0]))
stage.play(VGroup(docs[1], docs[2], new).animate.shift(1.1 * LEFT))
stage.caption("first in, first out")

request: what do the digits in 3406 mean?

beats.intent: The number 3406 with each digit in its own column: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones
beats.narration: Each digit's position gives it a value: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
beats.code:
stage.title("Place value")
cols = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=1.6, height=1.2, color=GREY_B) for _ in range(4)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([0, 1.2, 0])
stage.play(Create(cols))
stage.add(cols)
for c, d, name in zip(cols, "3406", ["thousands", "hundreds", "tens", "ones"]):
    t = Text(d, font_size=48).move_to(c)
    stage.add(t)
    stage.play(FadeIn(t), run_time=0.2)
    stage.label(c, name, direction=UP)

beats.narration: So the three is worth three thousand, the four four hundred, the zero holds the tens place empty, and the six is six.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [3000, 400, 0, 6], labels=["3 thousands", "4 hundreds", "0 tens", "6 ones"], color=BLUE)

beats.narration: Add the values back up and you get the number.
